body:
Bumps [boto3](https://github.com/boto/boto3) from 1.16.22 to 1.17.48.
Changelog

Sourced from boto3's changelog.

1.17.48

  • api-change:lookoutequipment: [botocore] This release introduces support for Amazon Lookout for Equipment.
  • api-change:kinesis-video-archived-media: [botocore] Documentation updates for archived.kinesisvideo
  • api-change:robomaker: [botocore] This release allows RoboMaker customers to specify custom tools to run with their simulation job
  • api-change:appstream: [botocore] This release provides support for image updates
  • api-change:ram: [botocore] Documentation updates for AWS RAM resource sharing
  • api-change:customer-profiles: [botocore] Documentation updates for Put-Integration API
  • api-change:autoscaling: [botocore] Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling announces Warm Pools that help applications to scale out faster by pre-initializing EC2 instances and save money by requiring fewer continuously running instances

1.17.47

  • api-change:storagegateway: [botocore] File Gateway APIs now support FSx for Windows as a cloud storage.
  • api-change:accessanalyzer: [botocore] IAM Access Analyzer now analyzes your CloudTrail events to identify actions and services that have been used by an IAM entity (user or role) and generates an IAM policy that is based on that activity.
  • api-change:elasticache: [botocore] This release adds tagging support for all AWS ElastiCache resources except Global Replication Groups.
  • api-change:ivs: [botocore] This release adds support for the Auto-Record to S3 feature. Amazon IVS now enables you to save your live video to Amazon S3.
  • api-change:mgn: [botocore] Add new service - Application Migration Service.

Census recently adjusted the API to allow for statewide block group pulls for ACS endyears 2013 and later, and for the 2000 and 2010 Decennial Censuses (blocks too!).  The logic for this is slightly different than what we generally handle in tidycensus so I've made some adjustments.  It's working so far: 

```r
get_acs(
  geography = "block group",
  state = "AL",
  variables = "B01003_001"
)
```

author: blaxill
body: A bit of an extraction experiment: Having `nats` in extraction code is slow. This includes as constants and indices to vectors. I only modified SubBytes here as it was the easiest to modify, but it knocked 20s off `ghc --make`. Test vectors for `MixColumns` and `AddRoundKeyNetlist` are unmodified (they include vecs with nat indices) and still extract slow. Parallel ghc (`ghc -j`) halves the execution time.

author: dstillman
body:
Follow-up to #1827 with [a bunch of conflicts resolved](https://gist.github.com/dstillman/d1e1bcbf6eb9180e9702319ab6b7493f), so it can be tested with current databases. I think it'll be easiest to leave the original commits alone and just push additional fixes here.

This is awesome! I haven't really studied the code yet beyond what was necessary for fixing conflicts, but some things I found while trying it:

- Page Down moves the selection instead of just scrolling
- "Title" shouldn't be an option in the column picker. It contains the twisty and shouldn't be able to be hidden.
- "Restore Column Order" is missing in the column picker, so there's just a separator at the bottom:

![columnpicker-separator](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/783082/114098672-b0452980-988f-11eb-832b-f329e86a36d5.png)

- Header separators are sometimes misaligned:

![misaligned-column](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/783082/114098731-c5ba5380-988f-11eb-9cc5-3813e41dbdea.png)

![advanced-search-column-misalignment](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/783082/114098754-ceab2500-988f-11eb-8fd5-93c761b2318c.png)

- For the warning about pref size, can/should we just persist to a dedicated file, as it says?
- We should plan to support configurable columns in Advanced Search, which is a common, extremely longstanding request. Where should we persist that?
- The Advanced Search window opened for me with the tree hidden. I can expand it, but that should have a minimum height — it shouldn't even be possible to collapse that completely:

![collapsed-advanced-search-tree](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/783082/114099185-6741a500-9890-11eb-8879-0531aff62144.png)

- When pressing "-" with a child item selected, the parent row should be selected and kept in view. Currently selection is lost.
- The selected row isn't being calculated properly after pressing "+" to expand all items. Down-arrow scrolls way up and selects the wrong row.
- +/- in the collections tree is extremely slow for me for some reason — takes almost 5 seconds, with pinwheel. Items tree, with thousands more rows, is much faster.
- "Loading items…" in the Advanced Search window shows up in the top-left corner
- Something weird is going on when I try to drag a child note out from under a parent item. The hover effects for both making a standalone item and for dragging to another item seem wrong:

![row-hover](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/783082/114099161-5f820080-9890-11eb-861e-616261787210.png)

- The alternate-row shading of the first row changes when I expand an item lower in the list:

![alt1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/783082/114099225-71fc3a00-9890-11eb-9451-ea5fb1354cb3.png)
![alt2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/783082/114099232-73c5fd80-9890-11eb-954c-c48dcdf56d91.png)

- After changing the column order such that the selected row isn't at the top, Home doesn't select the first row (though down-arrow does select the second row)
- Double-clicking a row isn't opening the PDF

I added everything need to make a Debian package.

Hopefully, I didn't break anything,
